drivers.evidence: Past price hikes: median x0.90 vs baseline; 1 occurrence, noisy, so shrink to x0.90.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 25.1. A store closure on Monday (Halloween week) reduces demand; past closures show a median x0.85 effect. Halloween itself has a noise-adjusted effect of x1.0, so no uplift. The price increase to $13.93 (+4.1%) likely suppresses demand; past price hikes show a median x0.90 effect. No promotion is scheduled. The classical model suggests x1.00, but judgment overrides: closure and price increase reduce forecast. Effects are multiplicative, but evidence is thin (one closure, one price change). Shrink toward 1.0. Final median adjusted down.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 25.1 | 5%-95%: 0.6 - 58.3 | 10%-90%: 5.7 - 41.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-77% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
